blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a key limitation of Deep Q Networks (DQNs): their inability to perform long-range planning, exemplified by poor performance on the Atari game Frostbite. The paper introduces STRAW (STRategic Attentive Writer), a novel deep recurrent neural network architecture that learns 'macro-actions'—sequences of actions based on rewards—and dynamically decides when to stick with or abandon a plan. Unlike traditional reinforcement learning approaches that output single actions, STRAW generates multi-step action plans, enabling more natural decision-making. On Frostbite, STRAW achieves a score of 8108 compared to a baseline of 1281, demonstrating its effectiveness. The architecture consists of an action module for planning and a commitment module for deciding plan adherence, with differentiable attention mechanisms to focus on relevant parts of the plan. The authors also explore STRAW's performance in text prediction, maze navigation, and other Atari games, showing its ability to learn temporal abstractions and outperform baselines like LSTM.
paper_title: Strategic Attentive Writer for Learning Macro-Actions
paper_abstract: We present a novel deep recurrent neural network architecture that learns to build implicit plans in an end-to-end manner by purely interacting with an environment in reinforcement learning setting. The network builds an internal plan, which is continuously updated upon observation of the next input from the environment. It can also partition this internal representation into contiguous sub- sequences by learning for how long the plan can be committed to – i.e. followed without re-planing. Combining these properties, the proposed model, dubbed STRategic Attentive Writer (STRAW) can learn high-level, temporally abstracted macro- actions of varying lengths that are solely learnt from data without any prior information. These macro-actions enable both structured exploration and economic computation. We experimentally demonstrate that STRAW delivers strong improvements on several ATARI games by employing temporally extended planning strategies (e.g. Ms. Pacman and Frostbite). It is at the same time a general algorithm that can be applied on any sequence data. To that end, we also show that when trained on text prediction task, STRAW naturally predicts frequent n-grams (instead of macroactions), demonstrating the generality of the approach.
